newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Coffee - Indonesia prices consolidate, demand dull.
newsitem.headline: Coffee - Indonesia prices consolidate, demand dull.

text.p: Indonesian coffee prices were consolidating on Monday as harvests drew to a close and well-covered buyers showed little interest, traders said.
They said grade four Robusta was quoted at 2,600-2,700 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 2,700 rupiah a week ago.
The export price fob Lampung was around $1,200/tonne against last week's $1,180.
"Buyers seemed to be fully booked and are only looking for long-term purchases," one Lampung trader said. "Demand is very thin and it looks like it's going to be a quiet week."
A Jakarta trader said prices were consolidating with harvests coming to an end and that farmers were still holding on to some beans, waiting for the right price.
"There is no selling pressure. The market will be moving sideways as there will be not much to sell soon," he said.
Traders said the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) meeting in London last Saturday had no impact on the local market.
The ACPC said the group's exports in 1995/96 (July/June) reached 44.83 million 60-kg bags against a target of 45.8 million.
"Even though (ACPC) members' exports were below the target, the news did not seem to support prices," one trader said. "So, I wouldn't exactly say it was good news."

Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, told Reuters in London that Indonesia's coffee production was expected to rise to 500,000 tonnes in 1997/98 (Oct/Sept) from an estimated 480,000 in 1996/97.
Soedargo said domestic consumption was expected to remain at 120,000 tonnes.
